# pbs_tasks (Data Source)

Lists the worker tasks of a Proxmox Backup Server node — backups, garbage collections, verifications, prunes, syncs and the other work PBS does in the background — as Administration → Tasks shows them: running tasks first, the most recently started first, then finished tasks, the most recently ended first. It is meant for `check` blocks and outputs: whether a task failed lately, when a datastore was last verified, whether anything runs before maintenance. It reads what PBS has when Terraform reads it, on every plan, and never waits for a task; the actions that start a task wait for it. Use `plantimestamp()` in `since` rather than `timestamp()`, which is known only on apply and puts the read off until then.

Times are in RFC 3339 format, for `timecmp()` and `timeadd()`, unlike the seconds since the Unix epoch of `pbs_gc_status`. There is no filter by job: the tasks of a sync or verify job are those whose `worker_id` ends in `:<job>`, such as `[for t in data.pbs_tasks.this.tasks : t if endswith(coalesce(t.worker_id, "-"), ":nightly")]`.

PBS keeps finished tasks in its task archive: with `task_log_max_days` of `pbs_node_config` set, for at least that many days, however many tasks that is; without it, the most recent 20 files of up to 512 KiB, more than 100 000 tasks. It removes a task's log with the task.

PBS lists only the tasks the provider's user or API token may see, and leaves out the others without an error. With `Sys.Audit` on `/system/tasks` — the `Audit` or `Admin` role on `/`, `/system` or `/system/tasks`, with propagation, as ACL entries have by default — it sees every task. Without it, it sees the tasks it started itself — a user also those of its API tokens, a token only its own — and the tasks of jobs it holds the privileges of: sync jobs (`Datastore.Backup` on the local datastore, and `Remote.Read` on the remote datastore or, for a local job, `Datastore.Backup` on the source; PBS checks these for push jobs too), verify jobs (`Datastore.Verify` on the datastore), and garbage collection, prunes and prune jobs (`Datastore.Modify` on the datastore). Scheduled runs belong to `root@pam`. `Datastore.Audit` shows no task of anyone else: backups, restores and verifications started by others stay hidden. `sees_all_tasks` of `pbs_tasks` tells which case applies, as `pbs_permissions` with `path = "/system/tasks"` does.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A warning in every plan when a PBS task failed in the last day, or PBS
# lost track of one. Without Sys.Audit on /system/tasks, PBS leaves out the
# tasks of others, such as scheduled jobs, which run as root@pam: the first
# assertion catches that.
check "pbs_failed_tasks" {
  data "pbs_tasks" "failed" {
    status = ["error", "unknown"]
    since  = timeadd(plantimestamp(), "-24h")
    limit  = 0
  }

  assert {
    condition     = data.pbs_tasks.failed.sees_all_tasks
    error_message = "The provider cannot see every PBS task: give it the Audit role on /system/tasks."
  }

  assert {
    condition = length(data.pbs_tasks.failed.tasks) == 0
    error_message = join("\n", concat(["PBS tasks failed in the last day:"], [
      for t in data.pbs_tasks.failed.tasks :
      "${t.start_time} ${t.worker_type} ${coalesce(t.worker_id, "-")}: ${t.exit_status}"
    ]))
  }
}

# The last verify job run on store1, if PBS still has one.
data "pbs_tasks" "store1_verify" {
  store       = "store1"
  worker_type = "verificationjob"
  limit       = 1
}

output "store1_last_verification" {
  value = one(data.pbs_tasks.store1_verify.tasks)
}

# How the runs of the sync job "offsite" in the last week ended: the worker
# ID of a sync job's task ends in ":<job>".
data "pbs_tasks" "syncs" {
  worker_type = "syncjob"
  since       = timeadd(plantimestamp(), "-168h")
  limit       = 0
}

output "offsite_sync_runs" {
  value = [
    for t in data.pbs_tasks.syncs.tasks : "${t.start_time}: ${t.status}"
    if endswith(coalesce(t.worker_id, "-"), ":offsite")
  ]
}
```

## Schema

### Optional

- `auth_id` (String) List only the tasks this user or API token started, such as `root@pam`, which scheduled jobs run as, or `backup@pbs!ci`. A user ID lists the tasks of the user's API tokens too.
- `limit` (Number) How many tasks to list at most, the most recent first. Defaults to `50`, as in PBS. `0` lists every task that matches, which can be many thousands and has PBS read its whole task archive: combine it with `since`.
- `node` (String) Node to read: `localhost` or the node's host name. Defaults to the provider's `node`.
- `running` (Boolean) Whether to list only running tasks. It cannot be `true` together with `status`.
- `since` (String) List only the tasks that started at or after this time, in RFC 3339 format, such as `timeadd(plantimestamp(), "-24h")`. PBS stops reading its task archive at the first task that ended before it, which keeps the read quick.
- `status` (Set of String) List only finished tasks that ended in one of these ways: `ok`, `warning`, `error`, or `unknown` (PBS lost track of the task, because PBS was stopped while it ran, say). Running tasks are left out, so `running = true` cannot be combined with it.
- `store` (String) List only the tasks of this datastore, such as `store1`: its backups, garbage collections, prunes and prune jobs, verifications of every kind, and the runs of sync jobs whose local datastore it is (the target of a pull, the source of a push). PBS counts no other task as a datastore's: not restores (`reader`), syncs started by hand (`sync`), creating, removing, mounting or unmounting the datastore, or S3 refreshes. A datastore PBS does not have lists no task.
- `until` (String) List only the tasks that started at or before this time, in RFC 3339 format.
- `worker_type` (String) List only the tasks of this type, such as `garbage_collection`, `verificationjob`, `syncjob`, `prunejob`, `backup` or `aptupdate`. The type must match exactly: `prune` does not list `prunejob` tasks.

### Read-Only

- `sees_all_tasks` (Boolean) Whether the provider's user or API token has `Sys.Audit` on `/system/tasks`, and so sees every task; false when PBS leaves out the tasks it may not see. A `check` that no task failed should assert it too.
- `tasks` (Attributes List) The tasks, in PBS's order: running tasks first, the most recently started first, then finished tasks, the most recently ended first. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tasks))

<a id="nestedatt--tasks"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tasks`

Read-Only:

- `auth_id` (String) User or API token that started the task, such as `root@pam`, which scheduled jobs run as, or `backup@pbs!ci`.
- `duration` (Number) How long the task ran, in seconds: `end_time` minus `start_time`; null while it runs.
- `end_time` (String) When the task ended, in RFC 3339 format (UTC); null while it runs. For a task PBS lost track of, the time of the last line of its log that has one, or `start_time`.
- `exit_status` (String) How the task ended, as PBS words it: `OK`, `WARNINGS: <count>`, `unknown`, or the first line of the error; null while it runs.
- `start_time` (String) When the task started, in RFC 3339 format (UTC).
- `status` (String) `running`, or how the task ended: `ok`, `warning`, `error`, or `unknown` when PBS lost track of it, because PBS was stopped while it ran, say. PBS before 4.1 may report a task whose error has several lines as `unknown` too.
- `upid` (String) Task ID (UPID), which `pbs_task` reads the task by.
- `worker_id` (String) What the task works on, as PBS names it by type: the datastore of a garbage collection, `<datastore>:<job>` of a verify job, `<remote>:<remote datastore>:<datastore>:<namespace>:<job>` of a sync job (`-` as the remote of a local one, and the namespace empty for the root), `<datastore>` or `<datastore>:<namespace>` of a prune job; null for a task without one, such as `aptupdate`. The tasks of one sync or verify job end in `:<job>`.
- `worker_type` (String) Type of the task, such as `garbage_collection`, `verificationjob`, `syncjob`, `prunejob`, `backup`, `reader` (a restore) or `aptupdate`.
